description: Intelligent Agriculture Labs is a small team working where space data meets the farm gate. Satellites watch every field on Earth, but very little of that knowledge reaches the people who farm them. We close that gap by turning NASA's open data into short, trustworthy cards that say what's changing on your field, why it matters and what to do next. You can tap any card to see the evidence behind it. We design for real conditions: weak connectivity, many languages and decisions that can't wait.
summary:
IA · Intelligent Agriculture is a free web, iOS and Android app that turns 40 years of NASA Earth observations into simple, field-level decisions for farmers.

A farmer taps their field on satellite imagery and AI detects the boundary. Each week, IA gives at most three actions: when and how much to irrigate, drought status, and disease, pest, frost and heat warnings. Each one has a one-tap "Why?" that shows the NASA evidence behind it. IA also plans the next several years, checking the crop rotation against 30 soil-borne diseases and pests, nitrogen, erosion and water. It then suggests a better plan and shows its impact on water, fertiliser, CO₂e, topsoil and income.

To address the Field Shift challenge, IA combines NASA POWER, GPM IMERG, SMAP, MODIS, ECOSTRESS, GRACE, FIRMS and SRTM with established agronomic models, validated across many countries.

This matters because farmers face hotter summers, less reliable rain and declining soil, yet NASA's data rarely reaches them in a form they can use. IA works offline, in six languages, and fits each week's advice into two SMS. That makes space data useful to farmers anywhere, from Iowa to Kenya.
details:
What it does and how it works 

IA · Intelligent Agriculture turns 40 years of NASA Earth observations into weekly, field-level decisions. A farmer taps inside their field on satellite imagery, and an AI edge model detects the boundary. IA then works in five tabs:

  • Today: at most three actions for this week, ranked by urgency. A daily FAO-56 root-zone water balance runs on NASA POWER weather (1984 to today), uses a 16-day forecast and a Sentinel-2 crop coefficient, and says when and how many millimetres to irrigate. Drought status combines SPI/SPEI, SMAP soil moisture, MODIS vegetation health and a gradient-boosting classifier trained on U.S. Drought Monitor maps. Published models give warnings for disease (late blight, rusts, rice blast, coffee rust), pests (degree-days), frost and heat.
  • Field: 10 m greenness history, detected harvests, AI management zones, and terrain maps from NASA SRTM covering erosion hotspots, wetness, frost hollows and slope.
  • Plan: a multi-year rotation plan over 54 crops. It is checked against a cited knowledge base of 30 soil-borne pathogens and 22 rules, plus nitrogen credits, RUSLE erosion and water need. A beam-search optimiser suggests a better plan and shows its impact on water, nitrogen fertiliser, CO₂e, topsoil and income.
  • Insights: 40-year climate trends at the field, what-if scenarios and rotation comparisons over simulated seasons.

Every card has a one-tap "Why?" that gives a plain-language reason, charts against normal, a confidence level, caveats and the NASA sources.

Benefits and intended impact On the demo fields, the suggested plans would:

  • save about 9,300 m³ of irrigation water a year on a 5.5 ha Nevada alfalfa field;
  • keep about 530 t of topsoil over four years on a 48 ha Iowa field;
  • save about 50 kg N/ha over four years on a Kenyan smallholder plot.

These are model estimates, not yet measured on farms. The goal is to bring NASA science to any farmer on Earth, from large irrigated farms to smallholders on cheap phones, and to support their judgement, not replace it. Next steps are co-design with extension services and on-farm trials.

Validation

  • Reference evapotranspiration (ET₀) matches ERA5 at monthly r up to 0.997.
  • Drought status matches the U.S. Drought Monitor at ρ = 0.74 in Iowa.
  • Rainy-season onset is within 3.6 days of Indian Meteorological Department normals.
  • Yields are calibrated against FAOSTAT in 41 countries.
  • Field detection reaches IoU 0.52 in 20 countries the model never saw.

Weak spots and negative results are published openly.

Tools and technologies

  • NASA data: POWER, GPM IMERG, SMAP, MODIS, ECOSTRESS, GRACE/GRACE-FO, FIRMS, SRTM and GIBS. Partner data: Sentinel-2, ERA5 and SoilGrids.
  • Backend: Python 3.13 with FastAPI, NumPy and SciPy.
  • App: TypeScript with Expo and React Native for iOS, Android and web; Leaflet; i18next.
  • Engineering: Docker, GitHub Actions CI, and Playwright, Jest and Maestro for tests.
  • Development assistant: Claude Code. The app itself uses no generative AI at runtime. All advice comes from published, deterministic methods.

Creativity

  • IA turns satellite science into no more than three plain actions a week, each with its evidence one tap away.
  • A rotation planner reasons about soil biology and disease carry-over, then puts numbers on the trade-offs.
  • Tap-to-detect field boundaries.
  • Each week's advice fits into two SMS.

Factors we considered

  • Access: works offline, on low-end phones and by SMS.
  • Language: six languages including Swahili and Hindi, plus a plain-language glossary.
  • Trust: cited methods, confidence on every number, "needs local review" notes, and validation in many countries.
  • Global reach: uses only globally available data and local prices and sowing calendars.
  • Privacy: sharing by code works without an account.
